description: The bar chart illustrates the effect sizes of various linguistic features across different language families and a set of isolated languages, as measured by multilingual BERT models. The horizontal axis categorizes the data by language family, including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, and Uralic, while the vertical axis represents the effect, scaled from -5 to 35. Each category on the x-axis contains a group of bars, with each bar corresponding to a specific model and linguistic feature combination, as indicated by the legend: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (red). Error bars are included for each bar, indicating the variability or uncertainty in the effect estimates. The chart shows that the effect sizes vary significantly across language families and model-feature combinations, with the IE-Indic family generally exhibiting the highest effect values, particularly for mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂, which reach over 20. In contrast, the Isolate and Uralic categories show much smaller effect sizes, mostly near zero. The bars within each group are arranged side-by-side, allowing for direct comparison of the effects across different models and features within the same language family. The overall trend suggests that the choice of model and linguistic feature has a substantial impact on the measured effect, with some combinations showing much stronger signals than others.
